shortDescription: Japanese government bond (JGB) yields eased to multiweek lows in a quiet session on Thursday, as traders weighed geopolitical and inflation risks while looking ahead to next week's Bank of Japan meeting.

children: Japanese government bond (JGB) yields eased to multiweek lows in a quiet session on Thursday, as traders weighed geopolitical and inflation risks while looking ahead to next week's Bank of Japan meeting.

JGBs have benefited from safe haven flows in recent days, with price gains for bonds pushing their yields lower, as markets watch developments in the Middle East conflict, France's deficit and street protests, and swings in equities on earnings and AI news headlines
The benchmark 10-year JGB yield (JP10YTN=JBTC) fell 1 basis point to 2.88%, the lowest since September 9
The 5-year yield (JP5YTN=JBTC) dipped 1.5 bps to 2.285%, the lowest since September 18
The 30-year yield (JP30YTN=JBTC) dropped 2.5 bps to 3.895%, the lowest since August 6
Other cash bond tenors had not traded as of 0349 GMT
The BOJ is widely expected to hold interest rates steady on Friday of next week, although markets lay 60% odds on a quarter-point hike by the conclusion of the following meeting in December

"With the BOJ's policy meeting scheduled for next week, it's hard to imagine big movements in rate hike expectations today. On the other hand, reports yesterday indicated that a drone attack by the Houthis on a Saudi oil field caused multiple casualties, keeping concerns about escalating conflicts in the Middle East strong," said Mizuho Securities analyst Yuki Matsuda
